gates.sentence: The period of 428.8 days is 1.1 resolution elements from the nearest calendar period (one year); that is clear of it.
The observing pattern has 19% of its power at this period; the sampling does not explain the signal.

Removing any one of 8 years moves the phase by at most 0.02 cycles and the amplitude by a factor of 0.97 to 1.04; the most important year carries 19% of the evidence. The signal does not hang on one year.
The 2 bands in which the signal is visible agree in phase to within 0.04 cycles.
Searched alone, the first 70% of the time span finds the same period (422.9 days), and its periodic model predicts the remaining 116 points better than no periodic model (log-likelihood gain +36.3).
With the time axis warped at random, the search does as well as in true time 5.5% of the time; the variation does not clearly keep time.

sentences: The best periodic model has a period of 428.8 days and covers 6.2 cycles in 293 points over 2659 days; its fundamental has an amplitude of 0.95 in the standardised units of the merged light curve (1 is the object's own scatter), and 11% of its power is in higher harmonics.
Against red noise fitted to this object, with the search over 318 trial periods included, the probability of a periodic model this good is 1 in 1,001 (0 of 1000 simulated nulls matched it).
After recalibration against the whole population searched, the probability is 1 in 76,042.
For contrast, a test that assumes white noise would have given below 1 in a billion (1.6e-46); that number is not evidence, because the noise is not white.

what_would_change_this: New data are the test. If the period is real, the periodic model fitted now will fit data taken later better than red noise alone; if it is a red-noise bump, it will not. No prediction was recorded for this object, because it was not promoted.
